column.text: Bitcoin's push through $74,000 is a short squeeze, not a turn, and the tape should be traded that way. Short liquidations ran $17.7M against $7.6M of long liquidations, and one 40x BTC short sits just 0.44% from liquidation after roughly $39.09 million in cumulative losses. Meanwhile, the money that holds coins is leaving. Spot BTC ETFs posted −$95.0M on Tuesday 10 Nov, bringing the 7-day net to −$1577.8M. ETH logged −$1.3M that day (7-day −$551.1M), and SOL logged −$13.4M (7-day −$46.1M). Smart money on Hyperliquid is still net short BTC to the tune of $668M. The macro backdrop is hostile. Stronger-than-expected October CPI, at +0.4% MoM headline and +0.3% core, pushed the 10-year above 5.00%, and December hike bets have climbed as high as 96%. Dollar liquidity is contracting. The $580M–$600M in leveraged liquidations over four hours showed how quickly the floor gives way: BTC dipped under $73,000, ETH cracked $2,015–$2,053, and SOL broke $82–$84. Fear & Greed sits at 29. The regime is RISK_OFF. Keep the short bias and treat failed rallies as the better-odds trade. Longs need a real mechanism, such as deeply negative funding, a capitulation print, a demand catalyst, or a failed breakdown. Without one, this bounce is short covering, and it has to hold on volume or it reverses. Watch whether BTC holds above $74,000 on real volume. If it fails, expect a retest of the $73,000 area. Until ETF flows turn, the next leg down is more likely than the next leg up.
